- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and prices are trending down, model often overpredicts recovery; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overshoot.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overreacts with exaggerated upward momentum; cap forecast growth at 2–4% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8) and prices show mean reversion, model often fails to correct; apply a 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period price peaks (especially after sentiment shifts to positive); add 0.5–2% buffer to final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is low but price is rising, model often ignores sentiment and overestimates upside; reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment <0.3 and price > previous 5-day high.
